And at this time the Turcomans of the territory of Albistan entered our glorious monastery which is called the Monastery of the Cold Waters (Dayra d-Qarire);
and they killed fifteen monks in it,
most of them teachers, along with deacons and other subordinates.
And when they set their faces to flee, these accursed ones,
the Tatars overtook them and destroyed them all with the edge of the sword.
And thus Justice took vengeance on them after three days,
and with the death wherewith they had slain, they were slain.
Now in Melitene, when the report of the Sultan's defeat burst forth,
the Subashi Rashid al-Din, together with the rest of the palace retinue,
went by night into the royal treasury,
and the gold and silver which they found they divided among themselves;
and they opened the gates and fled toward Aleppo.
And also of the notables of the city, renowned men,
especially Christians who had the strength to flee,
went out of the city.
And when they reached the mountain called Bet Gawze,
a journey of one day from the city,
a detachment of Tatars overtook them,
and they slaughtered most of them,
and the sons and daughters they led away into captivity.
And only a few were saved,
and entered the city naked and barefoot.
Now the common people of the city—cloth-merchants, weavers, and the rest—
when they saw that the governors and leaders had abandoned the city and fled,
the Muslims and Christians assembled unto the metropolitan of Melitene,
Mar Dionysius, that is, 'Angur,
who was afterwards made Patriarch,
and they begged of him that he would take charge of guarding the city,
because he was an alert and energetic man.
And the Christians and Muslims took oaths to one another.
And all night they would patrol upon the walls and keep watch,
and by day they would sit at the gate of the city.
For they opened one gate only,
that of the Citadel (Resha),
or that of the Palace.
And the city remained in terror for about two months,
until the Tatars departed from the land of the Romans (Rûm).
And God helped, and they did not come to Melitene,
except for those only who were encountered on the road of the fugitives at Bet Gawze.
